cards.prompt: RPI Pharmaceuticals uses a Requisition Form custom object to order supplies. Employees create Requisition Form records. The supply manager then needs to manage these records and maintain data in some fields that should not be visible to other employees. Assuming that the field-level security is not changed, which configuration or feature would be advised to hide sensitive data fields from other users?
options: 2 page layouts
Dynamic Forms
2 record types and 2 page layouts
answer: Dynamic Forms
cards.why: This tests field-by-field visibility on one record page without touching field-level security (FLS, the profile/permission-set setting that truly hides a field). Dynamic Forms breaks the page layout's single 'Record Detail' block into individual fields and sections you place in Lightning App Builder, and each field or section can get a visibility filter (for example, show only when the user's profile or role is Supply Manager). That gives the manager extra fields while regular employees never see them on the page, with one Lightning page and no layout juggling. Rule of thumb: 'show/hide specific fields on a Lightning record page based on a condition' = Dynamic Forms. Remember it is a UI convenience, not security; real security is FLS.

translate.situation: The manager should see some fields; regular employees shouldn't see them on the page.
translate.feature: Dynamic Forms (field-level visibility rules on a Lightning record page).
translate.see: Same record page, but certain fields only appear when the viewer meets a condition.
translate.notOther: Two page layouts work but is the older approach; record types add processes and picklists nobody asked for.

cards.traps: Several options would technically work; pick the modern Lightning-native one (Dynamic Forms) over layout/record-type sprawl.
cards.strip: Record page · hide some fields from some users · FLS unchanged → Dynamic Forms visibility filters

wrong.2 page layouts: Two layouts assigned by profile would work, but it is the older, heavier approach and the exam wants the modern, recommended Lightning feature. Page layouts are for arranging fields per profile/record type.
wrong.2 record types and 2 page layouts: Record types exist to give different business processes and picklist values; nothing here needs a different process. Adding record types just to hide fields is overkill.

cards.prompt: Users have complained that the columns in the 'Recently Viewed' list view of a new custom object called 'Item' do not match the columns in the 'All Items' list view that was created by the Salesforce Administrator. What can the Salesforce Administrator do so that the columns in the 'Recently Viewed' list view matches those found in the 'All Items' list view?
options: Modify the search layout of the object
Modify the page layout of the object
Modify the list view layout of the object
Modify the recent view layout of the org
answer: Modify the search layout of the object
cards.why: This tests where the columns of the special 'Recently Viewed' list come from. Recently Viewed is not a normal list view you can edit; its columns are controlled by the object's Search Layouts (Object Manager > Item > Search Layouts for Salesforce Classic / 'Search Results' layout). Changing the search layout to show the same fields as 'All Items' makes Recently Viewed match. Rule of thumb: Recently Viewed columns = search layout; every other list view = edit the list view's 'Select Fields to Display'.

translate.situation: Make the default 'Recently Viewed' list show the same columns as a custom list.
translate.feature: Search layouts (Object Manager → object → Search Layouts).
translate.see: The object's tab opens with the columns you picked.
translate.notOther: Recently Viewed can't be edited like other list views; page layouts control the record page; 'recent view layout' doesn't exist.

cards.strip: List views · Recently Viewed columns don't match · can't edit Recently Viewed → object's search layout

wrong.Modify the page layout of the object: Page layouts control fields on the record detail page, not list view columns.
wrong.Modify the list view layout of the objec: There is no 'list view layout' setting, and Recently Viewed can't be edited like a normal list view.
wrong.Modify the recent view layout of the org: No such org-wide 'recent view layout' exists; the setting lives per object in Search Layouts.

cards.prompt: A new Sales and Marketing dashboard has been implemented for all sales users of Cosmic Marketing Inc. What is true regarding Lightning dashboard widgets?
options: A dashboard widget is a visual representation of data in a report
There are only 4 Lightning Experience dashboard widgets: bar charts, line charts, gauge charts, and donut charts
When clicking on a widget, users are always navigated to the source report
In Lightning Experience, the smallest possible widget that can be added in a dashboard is 1 row by 1 column
answer: A dashboard widget is a visual representation of data in a report
In Lightning Experience, the smallest possible widget that can be added in a dashboard is 1 row by 1 column
cards.why: This tests basic facts about Lightning dashboard components (widgets). A widget is a visual representation of data from a single source report (every chart, gauge, metric, or table on a dashboard is backed by a report). Lightning dashboards use a flexible grid, and the smallest component you can size is 1 row by 1 column per the key. Rule of thumb: one widget = one source report, many chart types, flexible size and click behavior.

wrong.There are only 4 Lightning Experience da: There are many more: horizontal/vertical bar, stacked bar, line, donut, pie, funnel, scatter, gauge, metric, table, lightning table, plus text and image components.
wrong.When clicking on a widget, users are alw: Clicking can go to the source report, a filtered source report, a record, a URL, or do nothing; the dashboard editor chooses the click behavior.

cards.prompt: G.W. Computing has a global customer base and its Salesforce Org holds over 5,000 Accounts, 15,000 Contacts, and more than 20,000 Lead records. There is a persistent complaint from the VP of Sales that the information on Account, Contacts, and Leads is not up to date. He requested their Salesforce Administrator to validate and update the data with the latest information. What should the Salesforce Administrator use to resolve this issue?
options: The Salesforce Administrator should validate the information with a third-party solution from AppExchange.
This is a cumbersome task and the Salesforce Administrator cannot do anything about it.
The Salesforce Administrator should find the latest information of every record and update it.
The Salesforce Administrator should use Data Loader to validate the information of each record.
answer: The Salesforce Administrator should validate the information with a third-party solution from AppExchange.
cards.why: This tests data quality and enrichment: keeping tens of thousands of company and contact records current with real-world changes. Salesforce no longer has a built-in enrichment service (Data.com Clean was retired), so the answer is a third-party data-enrichment app from AppExchange (Salesforce's app marketplace), such as D&B or ZoomInfo, that compares your records to an external database and updates them. Rule of thumb: 'is my data still true out in the world?' = external enrichment app; 'move data in or out' = Data Loader/Import Wizard.

translate.situation: Keep thousands of company and contact records up to date with real-world info.
translate.feature: An AppExchange data enrichment app (e.g., D&B Optimizer).
translate.see: Records get flagged or updated with current addresses, titles, etc.
translate.notOther: Data Loader only loads what you give it; it can't tell you what's out of date.

cards.strip: Data quality · keep 40k records current · real-world validation → AppExchange enrichment app

wrong.This is a cumbersome task and the Salesf: Defeatist answers are never right on this exam; enrichment tools exist precisely for this.
wrong.The Salesforce Administrator should find: Manually researching 40,000+ records is not realistic or scalable.
wrong.The Salesforce Administrator should use: Data Loader only imports, updates, and exports data you already have; it has no outside source of truth to validate against.

cards.prompt: New Computing uses Salesforce for managing customer support. There are more than 100 support cases open in its service cloud application. The Support Manager wants to ensure that if the support engineer does not start working on a case after 24 hours, an email should be generated for the support lead and the manager himself. What is the best way for the administrator to achieve this?
options: Create an escalation rule to generate an email.
Write an Apex class to generate an email.
Create a validation rule to generate an email.
Create a flow to generate an email.
answer: Create an escalation rule to generate an email.
cards.why: This tests time-based case handling. Escalation rules (Setup > Escalation Rules) watch open cases and, when a case meets criteria (for example Status still 'New') and has been open longer than a set age (24 hours), they run escalation actions: reassign the case and/or send an email notification to people like the support lead and manager. That is exactly 'not worked within X hours, email someone'. Rule of thumb: case + age/time threshold + notify or reassign = escalation rule.
cards.traps: Flow can do almost anything; when a purpose-built case feature fits (escalation, assignment, auto-response), the exam wants that feature.
cards.strip: Cases · not worked after 24 hours · email lead and manager → escalation rule

wrong.Write an Apex class to generate an email: Code is unnecessary when a declarative, purpose-built feature exists; the exam prefers clicks over code.
wrong.Create a validation rule to generate an: Validation rules only block a save and show an error; they cannot send emails or act on time.
A record-triggered flow with a scheduled path could do it, but escalation rules are the purpose-built case feature and the expected answer.

cards.prompt: Which of the following can be stored and accessed in folders?
options: Mail Merge Templates
Entitlement Templates
Reports
Email Templates
Dashboards
answer: Reports
Email Templates
Dashboards
cards.why: This tests which items live in folders (containers with their own sharing). Reports, dashboards, and email templates (Lightning and Classic) are all stored in folders, and folder sharing controls who can see or edit them. Documents are also folder-based in Classic. Rule of thumb: if you can 'move it to a folder' and share the folder, it's a report, dashboard, email template, or document.

wrong.Mail Merge Templates: Mail merge templates are uploaded Word files managed in Setup (Classic feature), not stored in shareable folders.
wrong.Entitlement Templates: Entitlement templates are Service Cloud setup items attached to products for support terms; they aren't kept in folders.

cards.prompt: Robin is a Salesforce Administrator. He has been asked to explain what can be controlled in profiles. Which of the following can be controlled through profiles?
options: Roles
Field Level Security
Page Layouts
License Type
Object Permissions
answer: Field Level Security
Page Layouts
Object Permissions
cards.why: This tests what a profile controls. A profile is the baseline set of permissions every user must have; it controls object permissions (Create, Read, Edit, Delete, View All, Modify All), field-level security (which fields are visible/editable), and page layout assignments (which layout a user sees per record type), plus things like app and tab visibility, login hours, and IP ranges. Rule of thumb: profile = what you can do and see in the UI; role = what records you can see via the hierarchy; license = set on the user.

wrong.Roles: Roles are set on the User record and control record visibility through the role hierarchy, separately from profiles.
wrong.License Type: The user license is chosen on the User record and determines which profiles are even available to that user; the profile doesn't set it.

cards.prompt: What are some differences between using the Data Import Wizard and Data Loader?
options: Data Import Wizard cannot export records but Data Loader can
Triggering workflow rules is optional when using the Import Wizard but not with Data Loader
Data Loader can be accessed by all users, but Data Import Wizard can't
The Data Import Wizard can only load standard objects but Data Loader can load custom objects
Mappings can be saved with Data Loader but not with the Import Wizard
answer: Data Import Wizard cannot export records but Data Loader can
Triggering workflow rules is optional when using the Import Wizard but not with Data Loader
Mappings can be saved with Data Loader but not with the Import Wizard
cards.why: This tests the classic Import Wizard vs. Data Loader comparison. The Data Import Wizard (in-browser, Setup > Data Import Wizard) imports up to 50,000 records into common standard objects and custom objects, but it cannot export, and it lets you choose whether to trigger workflow rules and processes during import. Data Loader is a desktop/client app that handles up to millions of records, can export and delete, always fires automation, and lets you save field mappings to a .sdl file for reuse. Rule of thumb: Import Wizard = simple, small, import-only, optional automation; Data Loader = big, all operations, saved mappings.

translate.situation: Pick the right import tool and know its limits.
translate.feature: Data Import Wizard (browser) vs. Data Loader (desktop app).
translate.see: Wizard: guided screens, optional automation. Loader: export button, save your column mapping for next time.
translate.notOther: The Wizard does load custom objects, and Data Loader is NOT available to all users (needs Modify All Data).

wrong.Data Loader can be accessed by all users: Backwards: Data Loader needs API Enabled and suitable object permissions (often admin-level), while the Import Wizard is usable by many users with the right permissions.
wrong.The Data Import Wizard can only load sta: The Import Wizard supports custom objects too (plus accounts, contacts, leads, solutions, campaign members, person accounts).

cards.prompt: What is true regarding using subfolders to organize reports and dashboards in Lightning Experience?
options: Subfolders can be created in user-created folders
A hierarchy of subfolders can be created to represent a logical structure
Subfolders can be deleted but not renamed
Folder sharing is at the root level
answer: Subfolders can be created in user-created folders
A hierarchy of subfolders can be created to represent a logical structure
cards.why: This tests report/dashboard subfolders in Lightning. You can create subfolders inside folders you created (or have Manage access to), and nest them to build a logical hierarchy (for example Sales > Region > Team), which keeps large report libraries organized. Rule of thumb: Lightning folders can nest, can be renamed by users with Manage access, and subfolders inherit sharing from their top-level folder.

wrong.Subfolders can be deleted but not rename: Subfolders can be renamed as well as deleted by users with Manage access on the folder.
wrong.Folder sharing is at the root level: The key treats this as false, reasoning that sharing can be managed on folders below the root. Current behavior suggests otherwise; see the flag.

cards.prompt: A Salesforce Administrator wants to give another user the ability to assign one type of permission set designated for certain roles. How can this be accomplished?
options: Change the user's profile to system administrator so that they have the ability to assign permission sets
Create a new profile and assign permission sets to it
Change the permission set settings on the object in question
Make the user a delegated administrator and enable the delegated administrator to assign the designated permission set
answer: Make the user a delegated administrator and enable the delegated administrator to assign the designated permission set
cards.why: This tests delegated administration, which lets an admin hand off limited admin tasks to a non-admin. In Setup > Delegated Administration you create a delegated admin group, add the user, pick the roles whose users they can manage, and list the specific permission sets they are allowed to assign. The delegate can then assign only those permission sets to users in those roles, without getting full admin powers. Rule of thumb: 'let a non-admin manage users or assign certain permission sets' = delegated administration.
cards.strip: User management · non-admin assigns one permission set to certain roles → delegated administrator

wrong.Change the user's profile to system admi: Gives far too much access and violates least privilege; the requirement is limited to one permission set.
wrong.Create a new profile and assign permissi: Permission sets are assigned to users, not profiles, and a new profile doesn't grant the ability to assign anything.
wrong.Change the permission set settings on th: Object settings don't control who may assign permission sets; that's a user-management power.

cards.prompt: A user has asked whether it is possible to manually edit multiple records on a single page and save the changes at the same time. Which features could a Salesforce Administrator use to enable this in Lightning Experience?
options: Enable enhanced lists
Give the user the 'Mass Edits from Lists' permission
Enable inline editing
Enable quick edit
Enable Bulk Record Updates from the settings menu
answer: Enable enhanced lists
Give the user the 'Mass Edits from Lists' permission
Enable inline editing
cards.why: This tests editing many records from one screen in Lightning. With enhanced lists (rich, sortable list views) and inline editing enabled (Setup > User Interface), users can double-click cells in a list view and edit several records, then click Save once for all. The 'Mass Edits from Lists' permission lets a user select multiple records in a list view and change the same field on all of them (up to 200) in one go. Rule of thumb: list view editing needs inline editing (+ enhanced lists in the UI settings) and 'Mass Edits from Lists' for multi-record same-field updates.

translate.situation: Change several records at once from a list instead of opening each one.
translate.feature: Inline editing + enhanced lists, plus the 'Mass Edits from Lists' permission.
translate.see: Pencil icons in list view cells; select rows and update a field for all of them.
translate.notOther: 'Quick edit' and 'Bulk Record Updates' aren't Salesforce settings.

wrong.Enable quick edit: There is no 'quick edit' setting in Salesforce; it's a made-up distractor.
wrong.Enable Bulk Record Updates from the sett: No such setting exists; bulk updates outside list views are done with Data Loader or flows.

cards.prompt: What options does a Salesforce Administrator have regarding setting the page displayed after a user logs out of Salesforce?
options: Display a custom logout page
Display the 'Home' page of a custom application in Salesforce
Display the standard Salesforce login page
Display the 'Setup' page of the Salesforce org
Display a custom single sign-on page
answer: Display a custom logout page
Display the standard Salesforce login page
Display a custom single sign-on page
cards.why: This tests the logout landing page. In Setup > Session Settings (or My Domain settings), the admin can enter a Logout URL so users land on a custom logout page, such as a company page or an SSO (single sign-on, one corporate login for many systems) portal. If no URL is set, users go back to the standard Salesforce login page (or your My Domain login page). Rule of thumb: logout goes to the login page by default or to any custom URL you configure; you can't send people to internal Salesforce pages.

translate.situation: Choose where users land after clicking Log Out.
translate.feature: Logout URL in Session Settings (or SSO settings).
translate.see: After logout: your company's page, the Salesforce login page, or your SSO page.
translate.notOther: After logout you're no longer in Salesforce, so app Home or Setup pages can't be shown.

wrong.Display the 'Home' page of a custom appl: After logout the user has no session, so they can't land on a page inside Salesforce.
wrong.Display the 'Setup' page of the Salesfor: Setup requires an authenticated admin session, which no longer exists after logout.

cards.prompt: The CIO of a technology company has directed the Salesforce Administrator to enable single sign-on with delegated authentication for the org. Which of the following are the benefits of delegated authentication?
options: It applies to all users once enabled
It can make the login page private and accessible only inside a corporate firewall
It allows the sending of authentication and authorization data between affiliated but unrelated web services
It can be configured to use a stronger form of user authentication, such as integration with a secure identity provider
answer: It can make the login page private and accessible only inside a corporate firewall
It can be configured to use a stronger form of user authentication, such as integration with a secure identity provider
cards.why: This tests delegated authentication, a form of single sign-on where Salesforce sends the user's credentials to your company's own web service (often backed by LDAP or Active Directory) to verify them. Because your own service decides, you can enforce stronger methods (tokens, integration with a secure identity provider) and you can restrict login so it only works from inside the corporate network, making the login page effectively private behind the firewall. Rule of thumb: delegated auth = Salesforce asks your server 'is this password good?'; SAML/federated auth = trusted identity provider sends a signed assertion.

translate.situation: Let users log in with their company credentials, checked by the company's own system.
translate.feature: Delegated authentication.
translate.see: Login goes through your corporate server, can be locked to the internal network.
translate.notOther: It's enabled per user (permission), not for everyone; 'between unrelated web services' describes federated (SAML) SSO.

wrong.It applies to all users once enabled: Delegated authentication is turned on per user via the 'Is Single Sign-On Enabled' permission on profiles or permission sets, not for everyone automatically.
wrong.It allows the sending of authentication: That describes federated authentication using SAML, a different SSO method.

cards.prompt: The sales reps of Cosmic Electronics frequently access Lightning dashboards to view insights related to customer opportunities. There are four teams of sales reps, and a custom field on the Opportunity object is used to populate the team assigned to the sales rep working on the opportunity. A sales manager of the company would like a new opportunity dashboard that shows data specific to each team. How can a Salesforce administrator meet this requirement?
options: Create a reusable Lightning dashboard and clone it for each team to show specific data.
Create a Lightning dashboard with up to five filters to show data specific to each team.
Create a Lightning dashboard containing widgets that show data specific to each team.
Create a separate Lightning dashboard for each team that shows data specific to the team.
answer: Create a Lightning dashboard with up to five filters to show data specific to each team.
cards.why: This tests dashboard filters. One Lightning dashboard can have up to five filters; each filter targets a field (here the custom Team field on Opportunity) and lets viewers switch the whole dashboard to show just one team's data. That avoids building and maintaining four copies. Rule of thumb: same dashboard, different slices of data by a field value = dashboard filter (max 5 per dashboard, up to 50 values each).

translate.situation: One dashboard, but each team sees only its own numbers.
translate.feature: Dashboard filters (up to 5 in Lightning).
translate.see: A dropdown at the top: pick 'Team A' and every chart updates.
translate.notOther: Cloning or building separate dashboards means maintaining four copies.

cards.strip: Dashboards · one dashboard, per-team view · team is a field → dashboard filter (up to 5)

wrong.Create a reusable Lightning dashboard an: Cloning creates four dashboards to maintain; filters do it with one.
wrong.Create a Lightning dashboard containing: Separate widgets per team means extra source reports and a cluttered dashboard; filters are the intended tool.
wrong.Create a separate Lightning dashboard fo: Works but duplicates effort and maintenance; one filtered dashboard is the efficient answer.

cards.prompt: A user has called you as they have forgotten their password. What should you suggest?
options: Tell the user you will send a temporary password to their cell phone via text message
Tell the user that passwords can only be reset by Salesforce Administrators and you will need to do it every time
Tell the user to reset the password themselves from the Forgot Password link on the login page
Tell the user to email Salesforce support
answer: Tell the user to reset the password themselves from the Forgot Password link on the login page
cards.why: This tests basic password support. Every Salesforce login page has a 'Forgot Your Password?' link that emails the user a reset link (to the email on their User record), so users can unlock themselves without an admin. Admins can also reset passwords from Setup > Users, but self-service is the first and simplest suggestion. Rule of thumb: forgotten password = Forgot Password link; admin reset only if self-service fails.

wrong.Tell the user you will send a temporary: Salesforce resets go via email link; admins don't text temporary passwords.
wrong.Tell the user that passwords can only be: False; users can reset their own passwords.
wrong.Tell the user to email Salesforce suppor: Salesforce Support doesn't reset your org's end-user passwords; that's handled in your org.

cards.prompt: Under which of the following conditions can a user NOT be deactivated?
options: When the user is assigned to an account team
When the user is selected in a custom hierarchy field
When the user currently owns existing records
When the user is the sole recipient of an email alert
answer: When the user is selected in a custom hierarchy field
When the user is the sole recipient of an email alert
cards.why: This tests what blocks user deactivation. You can't deactivate a user who is referenced in a custom hierarchy field (a special User lookup, like a custom 'Manager' field, that points to another user) or who is the sole recipient of an email alert in automation, because those references would break. You must first update the hierarchy field or add/replace the alert recipient. Rule of thumb: deactivation is blocked when something structural depends on that specific user (hierarchy field, only email alert recipient, default lead/case owner, etc.).

translate.situation: Know what blocks turning off a departing user.
translate.feature: User deactivation rules.
translate.see: Salesforce shows an error and won't deactivate until you fix the dependency.
translate.notOther: Owning records or being on an account team doesn't block it; a custom hierarchy field (a user lookup like 'Manager') and being the only email alert recipient do.

wrong.When the user is assigned to an account: Deactivation is allowed; you're given the option to remove the user from account and opportunity teams.
wrong.When the user currently owns existing re: Deactivated users can still own records; you can transfer them later. Freezing or deactivating doesn't require reassigning first.

cards.prompt: The custom object Job needs several custom fields added because of a Human Resources request. What is true regarding custom fields?
options: Once added, custom fields cannot be deleted
Once added, the field type of a custom field cannot be changed
Custom fields can only be added to custom objects
Custom fields can be added to standard or custom objects
answer: Custom fields can be added to standard or custom objects
cards.why: This tests basic custom field facts. Custom fields (ending in __c) can be added to both standard objects like Account and custom objects like Job via Object Manager > Fields & Relationships > New. They can also be deleted (and undeleted within 15 days), and their type can usually be changed, with some data-loss warnings and restrictions. Rule of thumb: custom fields go on any object, are deletable, and are type-changeable within limits.
cards.strip: Custom fields · where can they go → both standard and custom objects

wrong.Once added, custom fields cannot be dele: Custom fields can be deleted; they sit in Deleted Fields for 15 days before permanent removal.
wrong.Once added, the field type of a custom f: Most custom field types can be changed (Edit > Change Field Type), though some conversions are blocked or lose data.
wrong.Custom fields can only be added to custo: Standard objects like Account, Contact, and Opportunity accept custom fields too.

cards.prompt: Cosmic Retail's admin notices that the agent frequently invokes the wrong action within a Topic that has many available actions. According to Agentforce best practices, what is the most effective way to help the reasoning engine choose the correct action?
options: Rename all the actions using generic labels like Action1, Action2, and Action3 so they sort alphabetically
Disable all actions except one so the agent does not get distracted
Write clear, specific descriptions for each action and its inputs/outputs so the reasoning engine can match user intent accurately
Remove the Topic entirely and rebuild the agent from scratch
answer: Write clear, specific descriptions for each action and its inputs/outputs so the reasoning engine can match user intent accurately
cards.why: This tests how Agentforce chooses actions. Agentforce's reasoning engine (the Atlas engine, the AI that plans what to do) reads the Topic's instructions and each action's name, description, and input/output descriptions, then picks the action that best matches the user's request. Vague or overlapping descriptions cause wrong picks; clear, specific descriptions of what each action does and when to use it fix that. Rule of thumb: agent picks the wrong action = improve action and input/output descriptions (and keep topics focused).
cards.strip: Agentforce · wrong action chosen · many actions in topic → clear action/input/output descriptions

wrong.Rename all the actions using generic lab: Generic labels remove meaning and make matching worse; order doesn't drive selection.
wrong.Disable all actions except one so the ag: That breaks the agent's ability to do the other jobs; the goal is accurate selection, not fewer capabilities.
wrong.Remove the Topic entirely and rebuild th: Drastic and unnecessary; the root problem is descriptions, which you can just edit.

cards.prompt: The Account object has a one-to-many relationship with which of the following objects?
options: Product
Price Book Entry
Case
Opportunity
answer: Case
Opportunity
cards.why: This tests standard object relationships. One account can have many cases (support requests tied to that customer) and many opportunities (potential deals), each linked by an Account lookup on the child. That's a one-to-many relationship: one parent record, many children shown in related lists. Rule of thumb: Account is the parent of Contacts, Opportunities, and Cases.

wrong.Product: Products are a catalog not owned by accounts; they connect to opportunities through price book entries and opportunity products.
wrong.Price Book Entry: Price book entries link a product to a price book with a price; they have no direct relationship to Account.

cards.prompt: Global Insurance has recently switched to Lightning Experience. The sales manager would like the sales representatives to be trained on how the Sales Path functionality works before they start using it. He wanted to make sure that the Sales team will not have access to this component unless training is completed. Other teams from other departments, based on the user profile, should have an access to the said component like the Accounts Receivable team. What can be done to ensure that it does not display on the opportunity record page until sales representatives have been trained to utilize it?
options: Remove the component from the Opportunity page layout temporarily
Set the visibility setting of the component to hidden until the filter criteria are met
Modify the existing Opportunity record page and remove the Sales Path component
Create a new Opportunity record page with the component but do not activate it yet
Record pages cannot be modified in Lightning Experience
answer: Remove the component from the Opportunity page layout temporarily
Set the visibility setting of the component to hidden until the filter criteria are met
Create a new Opportunity record page with the component but do not activate it yet
cards.why: This tests ways to keep a Lightning component (Path, the guided stage bar) off the record page for one group while others still see it. Component visibility filters in Lightning App Builder can hide the Path until a condition is met (for example, user's profile isn't Sales, or a training-complete field is true). You can also build a new Opportunity Lightning record page that includes Path and simply not activate it for sales users until training is done. The key also accepts temporarily removing the component. Rule of thumb: control who sees a component with visibility filters or by page activation per app/record type/profile.

wrong.Modify the existing Opportunity record p: Removing it from the shared record page also takes it away from the Accounts Receivable team, who still need it.
wrong.Record pages cannot be modified in Light: False; Lightning record pages are edited in Lightning App Builder.

cards.prompt: Cosmic Travel wants to test its agent against a large, diverse set of realistic customer questions before a major release, rather than manually typing each test conversation one at a time. Which tool should the admin use?
options: Conversation Preview, run repeatedly and manually for each test case
Agentforce Testing Center, which supports batch testing
The Salesforce mobile app's offline briefing feature
The Setup Audit Trail, filtered to show only agent-related configuration changes
answer: Agentforce Testing Center, which supports batch testing
cards.why: This tests testing Agentforce at scale. Agentforce Testing Center lets you upload or generate many test cases (utterances plus expected topic, action, and outcome) and run them as a batch, then review pass/fail results, which is how you regression-test an agent before release. Conversation Preview in Agent Builder is for quick, one-off manual chats. Rule of thumb: many test utterances at once = Testing Center batch tests; quick check = Conversation Preview.

translate.situation: Test an AI agent against hundreds of questions at once.
translate.feature: Agentforce Testing Center.
translate.see: Upload or generate a test set, run it, review pass/fail results.
translate.notOther: Conversation Preview is one chat at a time, good for quick checks only.

cards.strip: Agentforce · test many conversations before release → Testing Center batch testing

wrong.Conversation Preview, run repeatedly and: That's the manual, one-at-a-time approach the company wants to avoid.
wrong.The Salesforce mobile app's offline brie: Unrelated to agent testing; it's not a testing tool.
wrong.The Setup Audit Trail, filtered to show: Audit Trail logs who changed setup and when; it doesn't run tests.

cards.prompt: How are relationships between objects represented on a record page in the user interface?
options: Using Master-Detail Links between objects
Using Lookups and Related Lists
Using Custom Lists and Relationships
Using Page Layouts and Profiles
answer: Using Lookups and Related Lists
cards.why: This tests how relationships appear on screen. On the child record, a lookup (or master-detail) field shows a link to the parent record; on the parent record, related lists show all the child records. For example, a Contact shows its Account in the Account Name lookup, and the Account page shows a Contacts related list. Rule of thumb: child side = lookup field link; parent side = related list.

translate.situation: See how a record connects to other records on screen.
translate.feature: Lookup fields and related lists.
translate.see: A clickable link to the parent (lookup); a list of child records at the bottom (related list).
translate.notOther: Master-detail is a kind of relationship, not how it's displayed.

wrong.Using Master-Detail Links between object: Master-detail is a relationship type, not the UI representation; it also shows up as a lookup-style field and related list.
wrong.Using Custom Lists and Relationships: Not a real Salesforce UI term.
wrong.Using Page Layouts and Profiles: Page layouts arrange fields and related lists, and profiles control access, but neither is how the relationship itself is represented.

cards.prompt: ABC Corporation wants to display different fields based on whether an account is a Customer or Partner. Which Salesforce configuration should the administrator recommend to achieve this?
options: Create a Visualforce page to display different page layouts
Create 2 record types and assign a different account page layout to each record type
Create a new custom object for Partners
Define 2 record types with different fields in each record type
answer: Create 2 record types and assign a different account page layout to each record type
cards.why: This tests the record type + page layout combo. Record types (different flavors of the same object, here Customer vs Partner accounts) control business process and available picklist values, and each record type is paired with a page layout per profile. Layouts are what hold fields, so two record types each assigned a different account page layout shows different fields depending on the account's type. Rule of thumb: record type picks the layout; the layout holds the fields.
cards.strip: Accounts · different fields for Customer vs Partner → 2 record types + 2 page layouts

wrong.Create a Visualforce page to display dif: Code-based UI is unnecessary when record types and layouts do it declaratively.
wrong.Create a new custom object for Partners: Splitting accounts into a new object breaks standard account features and reporting; partners are still accounts.
wrong.Define 2 record types with different fie: Record types don't contain fields; page layouts do.

cards.prompt: Emily, the Salesforce Administrator for Slidero Technologies, no longer needs several fields on the Job Application custom object when the application process changed. What is true regarding deleting fields?
options: It is possible to delete standard and custom fields
If a field is undeleted, the data is not restored
Deletion of custom fields can be accelerated using hard deletion to free up custom field allocation
After a field is deleted, it can be undeleted within 15 days before it is deleted permanently
answer: Deletion of custom fields can be accelerated using hard deletion to free up custom field allocation
After a field is deleted, it can be undeleted within 15 days before it is deleted permanently
cards.why: This tests the deleted-field lifecycle. When you delete a custom field it moves to Object Manager > Fields & Relationships > Deleted Fields, where it can be undeleted for 15 days (with its data restored) before it's permanently removed. If you need the custom field allocation back sooner, you can use Erase (hard delete) on the deleted field to purge it immediately. Rule of thumb: deleted custom field = 15-day recycle with data; Erase to purge now.
cards.strip: Fields · deleting custom fields → 15-day undelete with data; Erase frees allocation now

wrong.It is possible to delete standard and cu: Standard fields can't be deleted, only hidden or removed from layouts; only custom fields can be deleted.
wrong.If a field is undeleted, the data is not: Undeleting within 15 days restores the field and its data (some attributes, like field history and layout placement, may need to be re-added).

cards.prompt: The marketing team of Cosmic Learning Solutions uses Lightning Experience to manage campaigns in Salesforce. Each campaign has a lifecycle, and a custom picklist field is used by marketing users to specify the stage of a campaign. The Marketing Director would like to add guidance for the users, especially those who are new to the company, by providing stage-specific tips, best practices, and other company information necessary to move a campaign to the next stage. How can a Sales Cloud Consultant meet this requirement?
options: Set up Einstein Discovery to provide stage-specific tips on campaign records.
Use Lightning App Builder to add the Path feature that allows visualizing and tracking the stages of campaigns.
Create a custom Lightning component that can be added to the Campaign record page.
Create a new Path using the custom picklist field for the Campaign object.
answer: Use Lightning App Builder to add the Path feature that allows visualizing and tracking the stages of campaigns.
Create a new Path using the custom picklist field for the Campaign object.
cards.why: This tests Path setup. First you create a Path in Setup > Path Settings, choosing the Campaign object and the custom stage picklist, and add 'Key Fields' and 'Guidance for Success' (the tips, best practices, and links) for each stage. Then you add the Path component to the Campaign record page in Lightning App Builder so users see the stage bar and guidance. Rule of thumb: stage-by-stage guidance on a picklist = Path; create it in Setup, display it with App Builder.

translate.situation: Show new marketers what to do at each campaign stage.
translate.feature: Path (with 'Guidance for Success' per stage).
translate.see: A chevron bar across the top of the record; click a stage to see its tips and key fields.
translate.notOther: A custom component is code for something built in; Einstein Discovery analyzes data, it doesn't hold your tips.

cards.strip: Campaign stages · show tips per stage → Path on the picklist + Path component on page

wrong.Set up Einstein Discovery to provide sta: Einstein Discovery gives AI-driven predictions and recommendations from data, not hand-written stage guidance.
wrong.Create a custom Lightning component that: Custom code is unnecessary; Path is a standard, declarative feature built for this.

cards.prompt: The sales reps of Cosmic Solutions would like to view certain important updates about their leads and opportunities in Salesforce as soon as they log in and over the course of the day. These updates should include overdue opportunities, leads assigned to them on the current day, and opportunities with no activity in 30 days. Which standard Lightning component can the company's administrator add to the Home Page assigned to the sales reps for this requirement?
options: Recent Items
Today's Updates
Assistant
Today's Events
answer: Assistant
cards.why: This tests Lightning Home page components. The Assistant component shows a daily to-do style feed of updates: new leads assigned today, overdue tasks, opportunities with no activity in 30 days, deals past their close date, and so on. Admins add it to the Home page in Lightning App Builder and assign that page to the sales profile. Rule of thumb: 'daily list of overdue opps, new leads, stale deals on Home' = Assistant.

translate.situation: Reps want a to-do style heads-up when they log in.
translate.feature: The Assistant component on the Home page.
translate.see: Cards like 'Lead assigned today' and 'No activity in 30 days.'
translate.notOther: 'Today's Updates' doesn't exist; Recent Items and Today's Events show other things.

cards.strip: Home page · overdue opps, today's leads, no-activity deals → Assistant component

wrong.Recent Items: Only lists records the user recently viewed; no alerts about overdue or inactive deals.
wrong.Today's Updates: Not a standard Lightning Home component name; a plausible-sounding distractor.
wrong.Today's Events: Shows today's calendar events and meetings, not lead and opportunity updates.

cards.prompt: Sarah is the manager of a team of sales reps who collaborate on Opportunities. They are each awarded an appropriate share of the total sale on each Opportunity. Which of the following features should her company implement?
options: Opportunity Collaboration
Opportunity Splits
Opportunity Teams
Opportunity Revenue Sharing
answer: Opportunity Splits
Opportunity Teams
cards.why: This tests opportunity credit-sharing. Opportunity Teams let multiple users work on one opportunity with defined roles and access. Opportunity Splits then divide credit (revenue or overlay) among team members by percentage, totaling 100% for revenue splits. Splits require Opportunity Teams to be enabled, because only team members can receive a split. Rule of thumb: collaborate = team; share credit = splits (and splits need teams).

translate.situation: Several reps work one deal and each gets credit for a share.
translate.feature: Opportunity Teams + Opportunity Splits.
translate.see: A team list on the deal, and a Splits list with each person's %.
translate.notOther: 'Collaboration' and 'Revenue Sharing' aren't feature names.

wrong.Opportunity Collaboration: Not a distinct Salesforce feature; collaboration is done through Opportunity Teams and Chatter.
wrong.Opportunity Revenue Sharing: Not a feature name; revenue sharing is what Opportunity Splits does.

cards.prompt: What are some considerations regarding using Leads in Salesforce?
options: When a lead is created, it can be automatically assigned to a user or a queue
Leads can be individual consumers
When a lead is qualified, an account, contact, and opportunity are always created
Opportunities must always be created from leads
Leads can be imported or created from an automatic process
answer: When a lead is created, it can be automatically assigned to a user or a queue
Leads can be individual consumers
Leads can be imported or created from an automatic process
cards.why: This tests lead fundamentals. Leads (unqualified prospects) can be auto-routed when created using lead assignment rules to a user or a queue; they can represent individual consumers (B2C) as well as people at companies; and they can be imported (Import Wizard, Data Loader) or created automatically (Web-to-Lead, flows, integrations). Rule of thumb: leads come in many ways, can be auto-assigned, and conversion is flexible.

wrong.When a lead is qualified, an account, co: On conversion the opportunity is optional ('Don't create an opportunity'), and you can merge into an existing account/contact instead of creating new ones.
wrong.Opportunities must always be created fro: Opportunities can be created directly on an account without any lead.

cards.prompt: What Salesforce feature makes it easy for sales reps to follow your organization's sales process through visual assistance that provides guidance through each sales stage?
options: Workflow automation for opportunities
Sales Path
Flows for opportunities
Salesforce Mobile App Sales Chatter Feed
answer: Sales Path
cards.why: This tests Path (called Sales Path when used on opportunities and leads). Path shows a visual stage bar at the top of the record and, for each stage, key fields and 'Guidance for Success' tips, so reps know exactly what to do to move forward. It's set up in Setup > Path Settings. Rule of thumb: visual stage-by-stage guidance = Path.

wrong.Workflow automation for opportunities: Workflow (now retired in favor of Flow) automated actions in the background; it gave no visual guidance.
wrong.Flows for opportunities: Flows automate processes or guide users through screens, but the visual stage guidance bar is Path.
wrong.Salesforce Mobile App Sales Chatter Feed: Chatter is a collaboration feed, not stage guidance.

cards.prompt: Galactic Sweepers offers a weekly office cleaning service that is invoiced monthly. What should be created to represent this?
options: A Revenue Schedule
A Quantity Schedule
A default Quantity and Revenue Schedule
A default Product Schedule
answer: A default Quantity and Revenue Schedule
cards.why: This tests product schedules. A quantity schedule spreads when units are delivered (here, weekly cleanings), while a revenue schedule spreads when revenue is recognized or billed (here, monthly). When both delivery and payment timing need to be represented, you use a quantity AND revenue schedule, set as the product's default schedule so it applies whenever the product is added to an opportunity. Rule of thumb: delivered over time = quantity; paid over time = revenue; both = both.

translate.situation: A product is delivered weekly but billed monthly.
translate.feature: Product schedules: quantity schedule (delivery) + revenue schedule (payment).
translate.see: The product line shows planned delivery dates and planned payment dates.
translate.notOther: Revenue-only or quantity-only covers just one of the two timelines.

cards.strip: Products · weekly delivery, monthly billing → default quantity AND revenue schedule

wrong.A Revenue Schedule: Covers the monthly invoicing only, not the weekly delivery of the service.
wrong.A Quantity Schedule: Covers the weekly delivery only, not the monthly billing.
wrong.A default Product Schedule: Not a specific schedule type; schedules are either quantity, revenue, or both.

cards.prompt: A customer service manager would like to assign cases automatically to the most appropriate agent to handle the request. What feature could be used?
options: Case Escalation Rules
Case Assignment Rules
Email-to-Case
Web-to-Case
answer: Case Assignment Rules
cards.why: This tests case routing. Case assignment rules (Setup > Case Assignment Rules) evaluate new cases against criteria (product, priority, region, etc.) and automatically assign them to the right user or queue. For skills-based or capacity-based routing, Omni-Channel goes further, but among these options assignment rules are the answer. Rule of thumb: who gets a new case = assignment rule; what happens when a case sits too long = escalation rule.

wrong.Case Escalation Rules: Escalation rules act on cases that aren't resolved within a time limit; they don't do initial routing.
wrong.Email-to-Case: Creates cases from incoming emails; routing is still done by assignment rules.
wrong.Web-to-Case: Creates cases from a website form; it doesn't decide the best agent.

cards.prompt: Cosmic Solutions often has multiple contacts involved in a case. Which of the following is the most efficient way to show them in a case record?
options: Using Case Contact Roles
Adding multiple contact lookup fields to a case
Using Case Contact Relationships
Multiple contacts cannot be assigned to a case
answer: Using Case Contact Roles
cards.why: This tests linking several people to one case. Case Contact Roles let you add multiple contacts to a case and record each one's role (for example Technical Contact or Decision Maker) in a related list, without adding fields. It's the standard, scalable approach. Rule of thumb: 'many contacts with roles on a record' = Contact Roles (exists on Account, Opportunity, Case, Contract).

translate.situation: Several people are involved in one support issue.
translate.feature: Case Contact Roles.
translate.see: A 'Contact Roles' related list on the case: Jane (Technical contact), Bob (Billing).
translate.notOther: 'Case Contact Relationships' isn't a feature; extra lookup fields don't scale.

wrong.Adding multiple contact lookup fields to: Works for a fixed small number but doesn't scale and adds clutter; Contact Roles is the efficient standard feature.
wrong.Using Case Contact Relationships: Not a Salesforce feature; 'Contacts to Multiple Accounts' exists, but not for cases.
wrong.Multiple contacts cannot be assigned to: False; Case Contact Roles do exactly this.

cards.prompt: A Salesforce Administrator has created a 'Project' custom object and would also like to track Project Tasks. How can the Salesforce Administrator accomplish this?
options: Create a custom Project Tasks object
Check the 'Allow Activities' checkbox on the Project object
Check the 'Track Tasks' checkbox on the Project object
Create a lookup on the task object to the Project custom object
answer: Check the 'Allow Activities' checkbox on the Project object
cards.why: This tests activities on custom objects. When you create (or edit) a custom object, checking 'Allow Activities' lets tasks and events be related to its records, and adds the Activity timeline/related list to the record page. That gives Projects real Salesforce tasks with due dates, reminders, and reporting. Rule of thumb: tasks/events on a custom object = enable 'Allow Activities' on that object.

translate.situation: Log tasks against a custom object's records.
translate.feature: 'Allow Activities' on the custom object.
translate.see: The Activity tab appears on Project records; tasks can be related to a project.
translate.notOther: 'Track Tasks' doesn't exist; you can't add lookups to the Task object.

wrong.Create a custom Project Tasks object: Rebuilds what standard Tasks already provide and loses reminders, calendars, and activity reporting.
wrong.Check the 'Track Tasks' checkbox on the: No 'Track Tasks' setting exists; the checkbox is called Allow Activities.
wrong.Create a lookup on the task object to th: You can't add custom lookups that way for this purpose; the polymorphic 'Related To' field on Task gets the object once Allow Activities is on.

cards.prompt: What is true regarding Web-to-Case?
options: Case creation will fail if case validation rules fail when processing a Web-to-Case submission
Cases created from Web-to-Case are always assigned to a specific case owner
Cases created from Web-to-Case are linked to the relevant contact and account based on the customer email address
The origin and status values can be selected in Web-to-Case settings
answer: Case creation will fail if case validation rules fail when processing a Web-to-Case submission
Cases created from Web-to-Case are linked to the relevant contact and account based on the customer email address
cards.why: This tests Web-to-Case behavior. Web-to-Case turns a website form into cases (up to 5,000 per day). Submissions go through the normal save, so if a case validation rule fails, the case isn't created (the default creator gets a notice). Salesforce also matches the submitted email address to an existing contact and links the case to that contact and its account. Rule of thumb: web cases obey validation rules and auto-match contacts by email; you set a default Case Origin in settings, but status comes from the picklist default.

translate.situation: Know what happens when a website form becomes a case.
translate.feature: Web-to-Case.
translate.see: Bad data → no case created; customer's email → case linked to their contact and account.
translate.notOther: Owners come from assignment rules (else default owner); only Origin, not Status, is set in Web-to-Case settings.

wrong.Cases created from Web-to-Case are alway: Ownership comes from the active case assignment rule, which may assign to a queue; otherwise it goes to the default case owner.
wrong.The origin and status values can be sele: Only the default Case Origin is set there; Status uses the Status picklist's default value.

cards.prompt: An administrator sets up an assignment rule that assigns leads based on a number of criteria. What happens if a record meets multiple assignment rule criteria?
options: The record is assigned to the administrator
Salesforce records an error in the assignment rule log
Salesforce assigns the record that meets the criteria of the last rule
Salesforce processes the rules according to the rule order and stops when a record meets the criteria
answer: Salesforce processes the rules according to the rule order and stops when a record meets the criteria
cards.why: This tests how assignment rules evaluate. An assignment rule contains ordered rule entries; Salesforce checks them from entry 1 down, and the first entry whose criteria the record matches decides the owner, then processing stops. So order matters: put the most specific criteria first. Rule of thumb: assignment rules = first match wins, top to bottom.

translate.situation: A lead matches more than one assignment rule entry.
translate.feature: Rule entry order.
translate.see: It goes to whoever is named in the FIRST matching entry.
translate.notOther: Not the last match, not an error; the order number decides.

cards.strip: Assignment rules · record matches several entries → first matching entry wins, then stops

wrong.The record is assigned to the administra: No; matching multiple entries isn't an error, the first match is used. If none match, it goes to the default owner set in Lead Settings.
wrong.Salesforce records an error in the assig: There's no error; overlapping criteria are normal and resolved by order.
wrong.Salesforce assigns the record that meets: It's the first matching entry, not the last.

cards.prompt: As part of the request for Salesforce Outlook Integration, the Sales Director of the company wants sales reps to be able to create and see related Salesforce records and automatically associate emails to them from within Outlook. In addition, the emails should be logged as email objects and not as tasks within Salesforce. Aside from enabling Salesforce Outlook Integration, what other features must be enabled or set by the administrator to fulfill these requirements?
options: Enable Advanced Outlook Sync
Customize email application panes
Enable Email to Salesforce
Enable Enhanced Email
answer: Enable Email to Salesforce
Enable Enhanced Email
cards.why: This tests Outlook integration setup. Enhanced Email stores emails as Email Message records (a real email object with To, CC, body, and attachments) instead of Task records, which meets the 'email objects, not tasks' requirement. Email to Salesforce lets users relate and log emails to Salesforce records (it works with the Outlook integration to associate emails with related records). Rule of thumb: 'log as email, not task' = Enhanced Email.

translate.situation: Log Outlook emails into Salesforce as real email records.
translate.feature: Enhanced Email + Email to Salesforce.
translate.see: Emails show up on contacts and opportunities as emails, not as completed tasks.
translate.notOther: 'Advanced Outlook Sync' doesn't exist; custom panes are optional layout tweaks.

wrong.Enable Advanced Outlook Sync: Not the needed setting here; syncing contacts and events (Einstein Activity Capture / Lightning Sync) is a separate feature from logging emails.
wrong.Customize email application panes: Pane customization changes what appears in the Outlook side panel but isn't required to meet these logging requirements.

cards.prompt: A company that makes hiking apparel would like to collaborate with partners and find a way to be able to discuss various topics in groups. The collaboration is limited to discussions at this stage. What cost-effective solution would be recommended for this requirement?
options: Use Chatter External licenses for the external users
Set up a Customer community
Set up a Partner community
Create Chatter Free licenses for the external users
answer: Use Chatter External licenses for the external users
cards.why: This tests the cheapest way to collaborate with outsiders. Chatter External users (free) can be invited into Chatter groups that allow customers, where they can only see and post in those groups. Since the partners just need group discussions, this avoids paying for partner or customer community licenses. Rule of thumb: outsiders + discussion-only + cheapest = Chatter External in customer-enabled groups; need records/data = Experience Cloud licenses.

translate.situation: Let outside partners join discussion groups, cheaply.
translate.feature: Chatter External users (invited into 'Allow Customers' groups).
translate.see: Partners post and reply in specific Chatter groups, nothing else.
translate.notOther: Chatter Free is internal-only; a community costs more than discussion-only needs.

cards.strip: External collaboration · discussions only · cost-effective → Chatter External users in groups

wrong.Set up a Customer community: An Experience Cloud site with licenses costs money and is overkill for discussion only.
wrong.Set up a Partner community: Partner Community licenses are more expensive and meant for partners working on leads, opportunities, and records.
wrong.Create Chatter Free licenses for the ext: Chatter Free licenses are for internal employees in your company, not external users.

cards.prompt: An organization wants to explore pre-built AI solutions developed by trusted partners to improve their service efficiency. Through which primary locations can a user officially access the AgentExchange marketplace?
options: The AppExchange navigation menu and the Agent Builder interface
The App Launcher by searching for the "Agent Marketplace" application
The Salesforce Help & Training portal under the "Downloads" section
The Salesforce Setup menu under "Marketplace Settings"
answer: The AppExchange navigation menu and the Agent Builder interface
cards.why: This tests where to find AgentExchange, Salesforce's marketplace for Agentforce agents, actions, topics, and templates built by partners. It's reached as part of AppExchange (its own section in the AppExchange navigation) and directly from inside Agent Builder, where admins can browse partner components while building. Rule of thumb: AgentExchange lives within AppExchange and is surfaced in Agent Builder.

wrong.The App Launcher by searching for the \": There's no 'Agent Marketplace' app in the App Launcher.
wrong.The Salesforce Help & Training portal un: Help & Training hosts docs and learning, not the partner marketplace.
wrong.The Salesforce Setup menu under \"Market: No such Setup menu; the marketplace isn't configured in Setup.

cards.prompt: How many contacts on shared Activities can a user make as a primary contact?
options: It is not possible to indicate a primary contact on a shared activity.
cards.why: This tests Shared Activities, which let one task or event relate to up to 50 contacts. Among those contacts, exactly one is marked the primary contact, which determines the related account shown on the activity. Rule of thumb: shared activities = up to 50 contacts, one primary.

translate.situation: One meeting involves several contacts.
translate.feature: Shared Activities, primary contact.
translate.see: Up to 50 contacts listed; one marked primary.
translate.notOther: Only one primary; 'not possible' is wrong because one is required.

wrong.2: Only one contact can be primary on a shared activity.
wrong.3: Only one contact can be primary on a shared activity.
wrong.It is not possible to indicate a primary: False; one contact is always designated primary.

cards.prompt: What is the maximum number of items an administrator can add to a single Launchpad component?
cards.why: This tests the Launchpad component, a Lightning App Builder component that shows a grid of quick links to tabs, apps, flows, and URLs (often on the Home page). An admin can add up to 20 items, and only the first several show until the user expands it. Rule of thumb: Launchpad = quick-link tiles, max 20 items.

wrong.6: That's roughly the number shown before 'show more', not the maximum.
wrong.10: Too low; Launchpad allows up to 20 items.

cards.prompt: The Salesforce administrator has scheduled a data backup using the Salesforce Data Export service because they would like to download backup files from Salesforce to their local machine. How long does a backup data export remain available before it is automatically deleted?
options: 24 hours
12 hours
36 hours
48 hours
answer: 48 hours
cards.why: This tests the Data Export service (Setup > Data Export), which creates .zip files of CSVs of your org's data, either on demand (Export Now) or scheduled weekly or monthly. When the export is ready, Salesforce emails a link and the files stay available for 48 hours, then are deleted. Rule of thumb: Data Export files expire after 48 hours, so download them promptly.

cards.prompt: On what objects can duplicate rules be configured?
options: Lead
Custom Objects
Opportunity
Product
Contact
answer: Lead
Custom Objects
Contact
cards.why: This tests duplicate management. Duplicate rules (paired with matching rules that define what 'duplicate' means) can be created for Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Person Accounts, and custom objects, among a few others. They either alert or block users when a likely duplicate is being saved. Rule of thumb: duplicate rules = people and companies (Account, Contact, Lead) plus custom objects; not Opportunity or Product.

translate.situation: Stop people creating the same record twice.
translate.feature: Duplicate rules (with matching rules).
translate.see: An alert or block when saving something that looks like an existing record.
translate.notOther: Opportunities and Products aren't supported.

wrong.Opportunity: Opportunities aren't supported for standard duplicate rules; deals are expected to repeat across accounts.
wrong.Product: Products aren't supported for duplicate rules.

cards.prompt: The marketing team of ZS Global uses Salesforce for managing its marketing activities. They generated a little over 213,000 leads across the globe with the latest campaign and want all those leads registered inside Salesforce. They requested the Salesforce Administrator to perform this task quickly. What tool should the Salesforce Administrator use?
options: Use the Data Import Wizard
Contact Salesforce Support for data import
Create Records Manually
Use Salesforce Data Loader
answer: Use Salesforce Data Loader
cards.why: This tests the import tool size cutoff. The Data Import Wizard handles up to 50,000 records per import; 213,000 leads is well beyond that. Data Loader handles up to 5 million records and is built for bulk loads, so it's the right tool. Rule of thumb: over 50,000 records (or need to export/delete) = Data Loader.
cards.strip: Data import · 213,000 leads · fast → Data Loader (Import Wizard caps at 50k)

wrong.Use the Data Import Wizard: Limited to 50,000 records per import, far under 213,000.
wrong.Contact Salesforce Support for data impo: Support doesn't do routine data loads; admins do it with Data Loader.
wrong.Create Records Manually: Impossible to do quickly for 213,000 records.

cards.prompt: When an Opportunity Stage is updated to 'Closed Won', the Sales team would like to ensure that no users except the VP of Sales can delete that Opportunity record from the system. What can the Salesforce Administrator customize to achieve this?
options: Create a dynamic action with a filter for the Opportunity Stage and role
Create an approval process to lock the record once the Stage field is updated
Create an assignment rule to assign record deletion for VP of sales
Disable the delete button on the current page layout for other users
answer: Create a dynamic action with a filter for the Opportunity Stage and role
cards.why: This tests dynamic actions on Lightning record pages. Dynamic actions let you control which action buttons (like Delete) appear in the highlights panel based on visibility filters, such as record field values (Stage = Closed Won) and user attributes (Role = VP of Sales). So the Delete button only appears on closed-won opportunities for the VP. Rule of thumb: 'show/hide a button based on record values or the user' = dynamic actions. Note this hides the button on that page; truly blocking deletes everywhere would need a before-delete flow with a custom error or permissions.

translate.situation: Only the VP can delete a deal once it's won.
translate.feature: Dynamic Actions in Lightning App Builder.
translate.see: The Delete button simply doesn't appear for anyone else on Closed Won deals.
translate.notOther: Approval locks are for approvals; assignment rules assign owners; layouts can't hide Delete per user/condition.

cards.strip: Opportunities · only VP can delete Closed Won → dynamic action filtered on Stage and role

wrong.Create an approval process to lock the r: Record locking prevents edits by non-admins, but approval processes are for approvals, not deletion control by role, and admins can still edit locked records.
wrong.Create an assignment rule to assign reco: Assignment rules only set the owner of leads and cases; they don't control delete rights and don't apply to opportunities.
wrong.Disable the delete button on the current: Page layout button changes apply to everyone on that layout and can't depend on the Stage value.

cards.prompt: What actions are supported for joined reports in Lightning Experience?
options: Rename and reorder blocks
Add up to 10 blocks of report types
Convert unjoined reports into joined reports
Create cross-block summary formulas
Update and delete records
answer: Rename and reorder blocks
Convert unjoined reports into joined reports
Create cross-block summary formulas
cards.why: This tests joined reports (several report blocks, each possibly a different report type, shown side by side). In Lightning, you can rename blocks and drag to reorder them, convert an existing regular report into a joined report via the Report format switch, and create cross-block summary formulas that compare totals across blocks. Rule of thumb: joined reports = max 5 blocks, cross-block formulas allowed, no inline editing.

wrong.Add up to 10 blocks of report types: The limit is 5 blocks per joined report.
wrong.Update and delete records: Inline editing isn't supported in joined reports.

cards.prompt: Kody, the sales manager at Orbitflux has created a joined report in Salesforce which he wants to export. In what file format would the exported report be?
options: xls
csv
xlsx
xml
answer: xlsx
cards.why: This tests exporting joined reports. Joined reports can only be exported as a Formatted Report, which keeps the report's look (headers, groupings, blocks) and is always an Excel .xlsx file. The 'Details Only' export (CSV or .xls) isn't available for joined reports. Rule of thumb: joined report export = Formatted Report = .xlsx.

translate.situation: Export a joined report to a file.
translate.feature: Report export: Formatted vs. Details Only.
translate.see: You get an Excel (.xlsx) file.
translate.notOther: CSV is only for 'Details Only' exports, which joined reports can't do.

wrong.xls: The .xls option belongs to Details Only exports, which joined reports don't support.
wrong.csv: CSV is a Details Only export option, not available for joined reports.
wrong.xml: Salesforce report export doesn't produce XML.

cards.prompt: A collection variable in a flow contains a list of names of supported shipping countries. A list of accounts needs to be generated where their Shipping Country does not exist in the supported shipping countries. How should this requirement be implemented in the flow?
options: Build a Loop that iterates the collection and queries the accounts during each loop
Use the 'Get Records' element and query the accounts using the 'Not Contains' operator
Build an Apex invocable action that can be used by the flow to query the accounts
Use the 'Get Records' element and query the accounts using the 'Not In' operator
answer: Use the 'Get Records' element and query the accounts using the 'Not In' operator
cards.why: This tests the 'In' / 'Not In' operators in Flow's Get Records element. You can filter Get Records so a field (Shipping Country) is Not In a text collection variable (the supported countries), and Flow returns all matching accounts in a single query. That avoids a query inside a loop, which wastes limits. Rule of thumb: compare a field against a list of values in a flow = Get Records with In / Not In.
cards.strip: Flow · records whose field is NOT in a collection → Get Records with Not In

wrong.Build a Loop that iterates the collectio: Querying inside a loop is a classic anti-pattern that can hit governor limits (100 SOQL queries) and still doesn't easily express 'not in any of these'.
wrong.Use the 'Get Records' element and query: 'Does Not Contain' checks whether a text field contains a substring, not whether a value is absent from a collection.
wrong.Build an Apex invocable action that can: Unnecessary code; the declarative 'Not In' operator does it.

cards.prompt: In a real estate application, if a listing is sold, the status of all the related inspections for the listing must be updated to 'Canceled'. Which automation solution should be used to meet this requirement declaratively?
options: Use an approval process on the Listing object that performs a field update action to update the related Inspection records.
Use Flow Builder to define a flow that iterates through the related inspection records and updates their status to 'Canceled'.
Use an Apex trigger to update the status of the related inspection records when the listing status is updated.
Use a scheduled flow to periodically check listings and update related inspection records.
answer: Use Flow Builder to define a flow that iterates through the related inspection records and updates their status to 'Canceled'.
cards.why: This tests updating child records declaratively. A record-triggered flow on Listing (run when Status changes to Sold) can get the related Inspection records and update their Status to Canceled (a loop or a single Update Records filtered by Listing ID). Flow Builder is Salesforce's main tool for declarative automation. Rule of thumb: 'when parent changes, update related children' without code = record-triggered flow.

translate.situation: When a parent changes, update all its children.
translate.feature: Record-triggered flow (Get Records → Loop/Update Records).
translate.see: Mark a listing Sold → every inspection flips to Canceled immediately.
translate.notOther: Apex works but isn't declarative; scheduled flows lag; approvals can't update child records.

cards.strip: Automation · parent sold → update all children · declarative → record-triggered flow

wrong.Use an approval process on the Listing o: Approval processes are for approvals, and their field updates can only touch the record itself or its master-detail parent, not child records.
wrong.Use an Apex trigger to update the status: Works, but it's code; the requirement says declaratively.
wrong.Use a scheduled flow to periodically che: Delayed and inefficient; the update should happen immediately when the listing is sold.

cards.prompt: Sales users of a certain company that offers professional services are allowed to adjust opportunity amounts when negotiating and trying to close deals with clients. However, if the deducted value is more than 10% of the previous amount, the record should be automatically submitted for approval first. How should this requirement be achieved using a flow?
options: Build a record-triggered flow and use the $Record__Prior global variable to determine the previous Amount.
Create a Formula resource that calculates the percentage of the deducted amount and use it in an Assignment element.
Create a Formula resource that calculates the percentage of the deducted value and use it in a Decision element.
Build a record-triggered flow and use the $Prior__Values global variable to determine the previous Amount.
answer: Build a record-triggered flow and use the $Record__Prior global variable to determine the previous Amount.
Create a Formula resource that calculates the percentage of the deducted value and use it in a Decision element.
cards.why: This tests prior values in record-triggered flows. In an update-triggered flow, the $Record__Prior global variable holds the record's field values before the change, so you can compare the old Amount to the new $Record.Amount. A Formula resource can calculate the percentage dropped ((prior - new) / prior), and a Decision element checks whether it's over 10% to route to the Submit for Approval action. Rule of thumb: old value in a flow = $Record__Prior; branching on a calculation = formula + Decision.

translate.situation: If someone cuts the price by more than 10%, send it for approval.
translate.feature: $Record__Prior (old values) + a formula + a Decision element.
translate.see: The flow compares old vs. new Amount and only submits when the drop is over 10%.
translate.notOther: $Prior__Values doesn't exist; an Assignment sets values, a Decision branches.

wrong.Create a Formula resource that calculate: An Assignment element sets variable values; it can't branch the flow to decide whether to submit for approval.
wrong.Build a record-triggered flow and use th: $Prior__Values doesn't exist; the correct variable is $Record__Prior.

cards.prompt: Universal Outfitter's administrator has created a new record-triggered flow on the Account object. The admin configures the Start element to trigger on the Account object when a record is created or updated. What happens to existing accounts once the flow is activated?
options: The records are processed only when they are updated and meet the flow criteria
The records are ignored as the flow only processes records that were created after the activation
The records are automatically queued and processed if they meet the flow criteria
The records are processed only if the 'Run on Existing Records' option was selected
answer: The records are processed only when they are updated and meet the flow criteria
cards.why: This tests when record-triggered flows run. They fire only on the save events they're configured for (create, update, or delete) going forward; activating a flow doesn't process existing records. An existing account will hit the flow the next time it's updated and meets the entry conditions. Rule of thumb: record-triggered flows aren't retroactive; to process existing records, use a scheduled flow or a data update.

translate.situation: What happens to old records when you turn on a new automation?
translate.feature: Record-triggered flow activation.
translate.see: Nothing happens to existing records until someone edits one.
translate.notOther: There's no back-fill and no 'Run on Existing Records' option.

wrong.The records are ignored as the flow only: Configured for create OR update, so existing records are processed when they're updated.
wrong.The records are automatically queued and: Activation doesn't trigger a backfill; only scheduled flows process existing records on their own.
wrong.The records are processed only if the 'R: There's no such option in a record-triggered flow's Start element.

cards.prompt: Which of the following are used while designing a flow in the Flow Builder?
options: Elements
Events
Connectors
Stages
answer: Elements
Connectors
cards.why: This tests Flow Builder's building blocks. Elements are the steps (Screen, Decision, Get Records, Assignment, Loop, Action, etc.), connectors are the arrows that set the order elements run, and resources are the variables, formulas, and constants that store data. Rule of thumb: flow = elements + connectors + resources.
